Each command runs in a fresh process that starts in the session working directory (a reused shellId keeps the directory its shell was created in) — environment variables and any cd do not persist across calls. For independent probes, use separate calls or ;. Prefer short inspect-then-act-then-verify loops over dense one-liner chains.

Set `detach: true` for long-lived services that must stay available after you return control to the user (e.g. servers, watchers, or watch-mode builds needed between prompts or for external use), or commands that must outlive the owning process. Attached services count as ongoing work and prevent the agent from becoming idle. A request to run or leave a command in the background is not by itself a reason to detach. Keep bounded commands attached unless they must outlive the owning process. Keep helpers used only for a self-contained check attached and stop them before returning control. Detached commands cannot run inside the sandbox; detaching requires approval to run outside it. If that approval is unavailable, keep the service attached and explain the limitation. If false or omitted, the async process is attached to the session: it keeps running across later turns and is terminated at session shutdown.
